references.text: The Lord predicts that Pharaoh will drive the Israelites out of the land with a strong hand, which is fulfilled here.
The Lord predicts that Pharaoh will drive the people completely out after the final plague.
Pharaoh had previously sent Moses away in anger, but now the Egyptians themselves press the people to leave the land.
The context for the Egyptians' fear - the tenth plague where all firstborn died, and there was great outcry in Egypt.
Egypt rejoiced as they left, for fear of the Israelites had fallen upon them.
God's covenant with Abraham predicted that his descendants would leave the land of oppression with great wealth.
Describes how the Israelites departed from Rameses while the Egyptians buried their firstborn.
Complementary scenes in the liberation narrative where the Egyptians' panic leads to both expulsion and their own flight.
Theological contrast between being driven out of Egypt (Ex 12) and fleeing back there in fear (2Kgs 25).
Parallel in the argument about 'dying': the Egyptians feared dying if the people stayed, while the Israelites feared dying because they were led out.
Ironical parallel: the Egyptians press them out for fear of dying, while the Israelites complain that they were led out to die.
